flexQuery.title: Flex Query
flexQuery.hint: The token and query id of this account's Flex Query at Interactive Brokers. Choose below who may relay the call.

flexRelay.legend: Who relays the call to Interactive Brokers
flexRelay.agentHint: The token and the statement go from this browser to the agent on this machine, then to Interactive Brokers. Nothing goes through the server. Without a detected agent, no synchronization.
flexRelay.agentAndServerHint: The agent relays when it is detected. Otherwise, and if you are signed in, the server relays the call: the token and the statement pass through it without being logged or kept. Lets you synchronize from another device.

import.title: Import files
import.hint: A Flex query response (XML) with the sections Trades, Cash Transactions, Corporate Actions, Open Positions and Cash Report, or an activity statement exported as HTML from the Client Portal, which also brings positions and cash as of its end date. Flex owns its own date range; a statement only fills the history before it. Several files picked together are imported in the order of their periods.

report.droppedHint: Flex replaced this range. Kinds listed here are not exported by your Flex query: tick their sections in the Client Portal or they only live in statements.
report.staleSnapshot: Positions ignored: the file is older than the cached positions.

purge.confirm: Delete this account's history ({{transactions}} rows), contracts, positions, cash points and import journal? Your {{statements}} kept statements, the Flex/TWS settings and the sector table stay in place. “Replay statements” rebuilds the history, contracts, positions and cash the statements brought; a Flex sync rebuilds its own.
purge.done_one: {{count}} history row and {{contracts}} contracts deleted, along with the positions, the cash points and the import journal.
purge.done_other: {{count}} history rows and {{contracts}} contracts deleted, along with the positions, the cash points and the import journal.

statements.title: Statements kept
statements.hint: Imported HTML statements stay in this browser so the history can be rebuilt when the file reader improves. Neither Flex responses nor the local agent are kept, and nothing is ever sent to the server.
statements.deleteConfirm: Delete the statement {{period}}? Its rows will disappear from the history.
statements.replayConfirm_one: {{count}} row of the history comes from a statement no longer kept: it will be gone for good. Rebuild anyway?
statements.replayConfirm_other: {{count}} rows of the history come from statements no longer kept: they will be gone for good. Rebuild anyway?
statements.error: Replay cancelled, nothing was written: {{fileName}} can no longer be read.

sectors.intro: The sector and the score of each ticker, in one table shared by every account. An Interactive Brokers import adds the tickers it does not know yet.

import.title: CSV import
import.hint: CSV separated by semicolons, columns read by name: Ticker, Name, Category, Score and Status. The file adds new tickers and updates the ones it names; a column the file lacks keeps its value, an empty cell clears it. No row is ever deleted.

what.title: The local agent
what.text: The agent reads TWS on your machine and talks to this site and to Interactive Brokers only. It stores nothing: positions, cash and today's fills never leave your computer. It also relays this site's Flex Query calls to Interactive Brokers, keeping nothing: in "local agent only" mode, the Flex token never goes through the server. Without it, the app works with statements, and with Flex Query if you let the server relay.
what.dayValues: Day chg and Daily P&L come from the local agent: a portfolio rebuilt from a statement or a Flex response leaves them at "—", as does a contract bought or sold today.

uv.title: 1. Install uv
uv.text: uv installs the agent and the Python it needs.

install.title: 2. Install the agent
install.text: The command installs the version this site serves. Run it again after the site is updated.
install.unavailable: This server does not serve the agent package: in development, run pnpm build:agent.

configure.title: 3. Configure and start it
configure.text: The first command records this site's address, the only one the agent will answer. The second starts it; leave it running while you use the site.

tws.title: 4. Set up the TWS API
items: Note the "Socket port": one port per account, each TWS has its own.
"Read-Only API" can stay ticked: the agent never places an order.

chrome.title: 5. The browser's permission
chrome.text: The first time, Chrome asks whether this site may reach your local network: that is the agent on your machine. Accept.

port.title: 6. Fill in the port
port.text: In Data sources, Local agent card, enter the account's TWS port. It is only needed for live data, not to relay Flex Query.
